en: O Śrīpāda, O Śrīvallabha, you who are eternally endowed with splendor; O God of gods, protect us, who have been granted by you!
O you of renowned glory, who removes the afflictions grasped at as real entities, lift us up from this terrible suffering; homage be to you! (1)
You are our mother, you are our father, you are our kinsman and our sovereign; you are our protector, the provider of security and well-being, and you are the true Guru.
O Lord, O Universal Form, you are our everything;
deliver us from this terrible suffering—salutations to you!
Swiftly remove evil, torment, physical disease, mental anguish, wretchedness, fear, and affliction— none other than You can do so.
O Lord, having seen us who are Your servants, deliver us from this terrible suffering; homage to You! || 3 ||
There is no other protector, nor giver, nor sustainer;
O Lord, you alone are our refuge and the remover of our suffering.
O Pūrṇarāta, show favor to Ātreya;
deliver us from this terrible suffering—salutations to you!

O embodiment of all bliss, grant me delight in the Dharma, right understanding, devotion to the Divine, the company of the virtuous, worldly enjoyment, and liberation; and grant me detachment from worldly existence.
Lift us up from this terrible suffering; salutations to you! || 5 ||
Whoever, being self-controlled, recites with devotion these five verses that increase the auspiciousness of the world, shall become dear to Śrī Datta.
Thus ends the hymn of prayer to Śrī Dattātreya, composed by Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
